name: MI-11
label: Likely D

key_factors: D+9 district lean in the Oakland County suburbs favors Democrats
Moss holds a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge over Baker, plus outside support
Open seat with no polls or expert ratings widens uncertainty
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean, Moss's roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage over Baker, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold of this open seat; with no polls or expert ratings available, the margin is trimmed slightly and the uncertainty band kept wide.
model.watch: Emergent polling showing Baker consolidating Republican support, or the well-funded independent drawing Democratic-leaning voters, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Michigan's 11th District, taking in Oakland County suburbs northwest of Detroit, leans Democratic by about nine points, and Haley Stevens's retirement to run for Senate makes this an open seat. State Senator Jeremy Moss has built a large financial advantage, raising about $1.5 million to Ethan Baker's $142,000, with roughly $295,000 in outside support behind him. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

Prediction markets price a Democratic hold at about 96 percent. A well-funded independent and third-party candidates are on the ballot, which could trim the two-party margin a bit. The forecast expects Moss to win comfortably, though the open seat and lack of polling keep the uncertainty band wider than usual.
